description.narrative: Contract related to: Ukraine Media Center Kyiv - Ukrinform - Special measure 2021 Country allocations to support national (local) CSOs, democracy activists and HRDs working on critical human rights and democracy issues in partner countries. It will be managed by EUDs (INTPA/NEAR) and cover 116 countries. The Covid-19 pandemic is having significant negative repercussions on human rights, democracy and the rule of law in many parts of the world  and on the space for civil society organisations active in the promotion of human rights and democracy. An urgent reaction is required in the third quarter of 2021 to limit the harm done and contain further entrenchment and worsening of the situation.  The overall objective of the action is the worldwide promotion and protection of: (i) human rights and fundamental freedoms; (ii) democracy; and (iii) the rule of law. The action will achieve this so by supporting and strengthening civil society organisations (CSOs), democracy activists and human-rights defenders working on critical human rights and democracy in non-EU countries. It may also cover, where relevant, the promotion of international humanitarian law. The action will mainly be implemented through competitive processes.This action will mainly be implemented by EU delegations in-country so as to: (i) better respond to the country-specific contexts; (ii) take into account the local challenges of the current COVID-19 crisis; (iii) be as close as possible to the needs of the rights holders; and (iv) promote a sense of `ownership┬┐ of the action among local actors. The grants will aim at implementing the priorities listed in annex III Annex of the Regulation (EU) 2021/947 in line with Human Rights and Democracy country strategies. Implementing these priorities will also contribute to the EU action plan on human rights and democracy 2020-2024. The actions financed under the country allocations will be in line with: (i) the relevant EU action plan for human rights and democracy; (ii) EU guidelines on human rights; and (iii) the respective Human Rights and Democracy country strategies. All actions will follow a human rights based approach putting people at the centre of actions and also focus on promoting gender equality.

comment.narrative: MCU made 5 consultations for foreign media within Outcome 2 Providing support to leading foreign media in communication with the government to create a favorable environment for constant operation in Ukraine. July MCU had a request for consultation from Kyodo News Japanese media Representative of Kyodo News Japan came to MCU with a consultation about opening a constant bureau in Ukraine Kyiv. The main questions were Where should they file the notification Do they need to pay corporate tax or any other special payment for opening an office and how much will it be and so on MCU gave all needed consultations and based on the previous agreement with MIP referred Kyodos request due to the agreed process.November MCU had 2 consultations. MCU has organized a consultation for a representative of FOX News and the Guardian. Previously MCU had first contact with Fox News in September 2023 and after that their representative initiated a session for detailed discussion. MCU has presented and provided all the steps and information. An illustrative example of a successful result is a case study from Kyodo News which is finalising its processes for further opening a bureau in Kyiv.December MCU provided another 2 consultations to representatives from Italian Corriere della Sera and Spanish El Pas media who visited MCUs event for fixers in December Consultation meeting for journalists and fixers on the procedure for establishing foreign media offices in Ukraine 07 December 2023. During training representatives from various media outlets showed great interest in the case and asked many questions. Representatives of the mentioned media returned to MCU with detailed requests. The consultants from MCU answered all questions and provided relevant contacts and information.

comment.narrative: During the project period 4 consultations were made. The first one was in February 2023 when the regional branch of MCU in Kharkiv sent a request to support its branch within MCUUkrinform and take part in a 2days marathon dedicated to the 1st war anniversary. Media Center Ukraine Ukrinform joined the marathon for assistance in inviting speakers announcing the event on its channels etc. It was necessary to support the new regional branch and its activities and pay attention to the media audience. Lviv and Odesa branches also joined this initiative. httpswww.youtube.comwatchviNevpyRpAlQThe second consultation was in March 2023 when the Lviv branch was relaunched. MCU provided colleagues with information processes and tips to assist journalists at the time.The third consultation was with Kherson OVA. MU received a request and provided consulting support regarding the interest of Kherson OVA from Oleksandr Tolokonnikov who was interested in the possibilities and conditions of opening a branch of MU South based in Mykolaiv. Representatives of the MCU conducted several consultations regarding the requirements and details of the activity.The fourth consultation was in January 2024 with representatives of the Lviv and Odesa branches. These branches required pieces of advice on how to reorganize their branches after the completion of the financing period. During a consultation MCU assisted in restructuring the team and its functions providing examples of costfree decisions to support primary tools without losing the attention of journalists in those points. Furthermore MCU has accepted examples of regional experiences useful contacts of local authorities and a database of journalists. comment.narrative: During the first three months of the project MCU team developed a photo bank website for journalists to share raw content provided by the military security staff and photographersfreelancers which can be used actively by all media community and let them avoid mistakes in visual materials supporting reports and fill the lack of access httpsphoto.mediacenter.org.ua . At the end of March the website was launched. From month to month the content team actively gathered photos from different regional authorities and freelancers and filled the site. Weekly announcement of new photo updates was provided by sending messages to journalists and fixers through all MCU channels Telegram Facebook and MCU websites. Additionally this tool was promoted through the Producer Department MCU where many journalists make requests daily. The general number of announcements spreading was 46. Total number of uploaded photos 1367. Total number of downloaded photos 864. The most popular topics of the downloaded photo were Ukrainian rescuers at work after a series shelling of Ukrainian cities Kyiv Kharkiv Odesa Lviv etc work of Mobile air defense units of the National Guard of Ukraine n in Odesa region russian pilot at a briefing at Media Center Ukraine Ukrinform in Kyiv September 5 2023 Consequences of the russian occupation in Irpin and Bucha and others. The site is easily searched by the English keyword photobank for journalists in case some foreign journalists want to find it through Google. The site has a strong navigation system using key tags so that journalists can find required content easily.Inconsequential noncompletion of KPI number of downloads is related to a startup period of site work as the first 2 months required time for promotion site among the audience and a lot of negotiations with photodonors about systematic sharing of photos with us.

comment.narrative: During the project period MCU arranged four media tours for journalists. However in the second year of the war it was difficult to find new and interesting locations for journalists to cover stories since the Kyiv Kharkiv and Kherson regions had already been visited and reported on extensively since they were deoccupied during 2022.However one press tour which was organized by MCU in cooperation with The Russian Volunteer Corps was held on a RussianUkrainian border with soldiers of The Russian Volunteer Corps and Freedom of Russia Legion in May 2023. This press tour impressed journalists as at that moment the MCU gave journalists a unique opportunity to receive direct comments from Russia Legion about the operation that occurred in the Belgorod region.Presstour 1 on 15 March 2023 MCU together with National Policy organized a presstour Presentation in the field of how police dogs detain criminals search for drugs and explosives and a demonstration of the work of mobile DNA labs of Kyiv region. Journalists could learn how mobile DNA labs work. Police officers demonstrated the work of mobile laboratories and forensic centers where experiments are conducted. 20 journalists joined this presstour.Presstour 2 on 17 March 2023 MCU together with National Policy organized a press tour on how police dogs detain criminals and search for drugs and explosives. 17 journalists joined this press tour.Presstour 3 on April 13 the MCU collaborated with the National Police to organize a press tour for journalists on the controlled destruction of antitank mines TM62M VOG25 and detonators for artillery shells in Kyiv region. The head of the explosive police service of the Kyiv Region Mykola Murai and his staff attended the event to provide detailed information on demining in the region. 30 journalists joined this press tour.Presstour 4 on 24 May 2023 MCU organized of a press tour for more than 80 journalists meeting with soldiers of The Russian Volunteer Corps and Freedom of Russia Legion. The gathering occurred at a secret location in the Kharkiv region approximately 30 km from the Russian border where journalists were delivered by bus. Considering the latest news about the offensive in the Belgorod region The press tour was promptly organized after the offensive began in the Belgorod region of Russia journalists were highly interested in this meeting. They had the opportunity to conduct the interview and gather more information about the goals of this operation. Over 20 media from 11 countries have been allowed to participate in this press tour.

comment.narrative: MCU held 4 meetings with the Ministry of Culture and Information policy.1st meetingIn May MCU conducted 1st meeting with the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy to discuss the possibility of allowing foreign media representatives to operate in Ukraine. The Ministry officials confirmed their complete support and willingness to assist. Furthermore they assured us that they have a specialized team to handle technical and legal matters related to this task. Moving forward MCU should compile a list of potential foreign media and initiate the negotiation process.2nd meetingIn August MCU and the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy signed a Memorandum. MCU has signed a Memorandum of Cooperation and Mutual Understanding with Ukraines Ministry of Culture and Information Policy. The purpose of this Memorandum is the cooperation of the Parties in joining efforts to promote the opening of a regional office of foreign entities in the field of media in Kyiv. The subject of this Memorandum is communication support for implementing the project Supporting the opening of regional offices of foreign entities in the field of media in Kyiv which is implemented within the framework of the Media Center Ukraine initiative. 3rd meetingOn August 9th representatives from MCU held a joint meeting with the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy of Ukraine and the Embassy of Japan representatives of KYODO media. Representatives from the Embassy of Japan requested from MCU how the process of opening a constant media bureau works in Ukraine within war conditions. MCU organized a joint meeting with the Embassy and the Ministry based on a reached agreement within a recently signed Memorandum. During the meeting both MCU and MCIP provided comprehensive answers to all the questions asked. Representatives from KYODO sought consultation from MCU in July on the process of opening a permanent bureau in Kyiv. This meeting was a continuation of negotiations involving MCIP.4th meetingOn November 17th MCU conducted final meeting with the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy to present of the Guide for Media Bureau registration which was made by MCU in the previous months. MCIP also gave their input about possible barriers to opening constant bureaus in Ukraine. One of the possible reasons why this process is so slow is the high price of insurance for journalists or any employee of such a representative office namely 6000 Euros per person. MCIP has published MCUs guide on their site httpsmcip.gov.uawpcontentuploads202311guideforforeignmediaoutletsrepresentativesinukraine.pdf

comment.narrative: MCU held 4 meetings with the Ministry of Culture and Information policy.1st meetingIn May MCU conducted 1st meeting with the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy to discuss the possibility of allowing foreign media representatives to operate in Ukraine. The Ministry officials confirmed their complete support and willingness to assist. Furthermore they assured us that they have a specialized team to handle technical and legal matters related to this task. Moving forward MCU should compile a list of potential foreign media and initiate the negotiation process.2nd meetingIn August MCU and the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy signed a Memorandum. MCU has signed a Memorandum of Cooperation and Mutual Understanding with Ukraines Ministry of Culture and Information Policy. The purpose of this Memorandum is the cooperation of the Parties in joining efforts to promote the opening of a regional office of foreign entities in the field of media in Kyiv. The subject of this Memorandum is communication support for implementing the project Supporting the opening of regional offices of foreign entities in the field of media in Kyiv which is implemented within the framework of the Media Center Ukraine initiative. 3rd meetingOn August 9th representatives from MCU held a joint meeting with the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy of Ukraine and the Embassy of Japan representatives of KYODO media. Representatives from the Embassy of Japan requested from MCU how the process of opening a constant media bureau works in Ukraine within war conditions. MCU organized a joint meeting with the Embassy and the Ministry based on a reached agreement within a recently signed Memorandum. During the meeting both MCU and MCIP provided comprehensive answers to all the questions asked. Representatives from KYODO sought consultation from MCU in July on the process of opening a permanent bureau in Kyiv. This meeting was a continuation of negotiations involving MCIP.4th meetingOn November 17th MCU conducted final meeting with the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy to present of the Guide for Media Bureau registration which was made by MCU in the previous months. MCIP also gave their input about possible barriers to opening constant bureaus in Ukraine. One of the possible reasons why this process is so slow is the high price of insurance for journalists or any employee of such a representative office namely 6000 Euros per person. MCIP has published MCUs guide on their site httpsmcip.gov.uawpcontentuploads202311guideforforeignmediaoutletsrepresentativesinukraine.pdf

This structured platform encourages active participation enabling all attendees to express their viewpoints and engage in meaningful dialogue with their colleagues. The session was intentionally devoided of broadcasts cameras and recorders fostering an atmosphere conducive to open and transparent conversations. The participants discussed Ukraines possibilities for liberating the region the most likely scenarios for the deoccupation of the peninsula and the key risks on the way to the reintegration of Crimea. Emine Japarova First Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine Oleksiy Danilov Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council Refat Chubarov Chairman of the Mejlis of the Crimean Tatar People and other representatives of Ukrainian state bodies international think tanks and nongovernmental organizations were present among the speakers. 82 participants were offline 27 participants were online. Representatives of 5 countries took part offline together with online participants there were representatives of more than 11 countries. httpswww.youtube.comwatchveqmMStUKOQEvent 2 Expert discussion How to sustain support for Ukraine facing a long war 30 October 2023 Oslo. Organiser Media Center Ukraine with the support of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine. Partners Norwegian Defence University College Centre for Defence Strategies. Format presentation by Ukrainian experts followed by an expert discussion and communication with media. Participants experts in security and foreign policy think tanks and representatives of the Ministry of Defence of Norway.Event 3 Roundtable Ukraine in War Is There a Winning Perspective and What Is the Strategic Goal of It 15 November 2023 Washington. Delegation experts Alina Frolova CDS Deputy Chairperson Deputy Minister of Defence of Ukraine 20192020 Adviser to the Ministry of Defence 20152016 Adviser to the Ministry of Information Policy 20162018. Oleksandr Khara a former diplomat and Fellow of the CDS. Advisor to the Minister of Defence of Ukraine 2020 a former Director of the Foreign Affairs Department at the Office of the National Security and Defence Council of Ukraine. A diplomat who held various positions at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine and Ukraines Embassy in Canada. The next questions were discussed Whats Ukraines theory of victory and how to address yet another wave of scepticism about Ukraines ability to withstand challenges Why is Crimea the center of gravity in this war
